title: Amazon Product Photos on White and in Use | AIVideosUGC
description: Create square Amazon product photos from one upload, including a white-background main image, a lifestyle view, and detail shots.
h1: Amazon Product Photos for Your Main Image and Listing Gallery
lead: Plan an Amazon gallery around a square white-background main image, a square lifestyle secondary, and a square detail or size image.
card: A clean white main image, then photos for size, detail and use.
intro: Amazon listings start with a square white-background image, followed by square lifestyle, detail, or size photos of this item. Keep the product recognizable from one view to the next, and use each image to answer a shopper’s next question. Build the set in order: choose the front-facing white main image, compare the same item in different colors when variants need clarity, then lay out the package contents or add a lifestyle and detail view.

It's made for sellers who need a fuller gallery without reshooting every item. Upload a phone photo of your product, pick a white background or describe a setting, and download the result. For front, side and back views, photograph each side and use the Every Angle template to keep the gallery consistent. Amazon's Sponsored Brands video and product-detail video have different upload requirements, so check the placement before adding a clip. Callouts and text labels go on afterward in Canva or another design tool.
specs: Square · plain white background · see category rules
Keep text and important details out of the lower-right corner
tips: Use a pure white background for the main image, and check Amazon's current rules for your category before uploading, since requirements vary by category.
Keep the main image free of added text, badges and props; save those for the other gallery slots.
Fill the rest of the gallery with a scale shot, a close-up of the materials and a photo of the item in use.

faq.q: Does this work for Amazon main images?
faq.a: Use square images by default: a white-background main image, a lifestyle secondary, and a detail or size view. Keep the product recognizable across the gallery and check the current category requirements before uploading.

faq.q: Can I add text callouts to my gallery images?
faq.a: Add them yourself in Canva or a similar design app. Letters drawn by AI can come out wrong, and a separate text layer is easier to correct later.

faq.q: Can I make a video for my Amazon listing?
faq.a: Sponsored Brands video ads require 16:9 and 6–45 seconds, with text and key details kept out of the lower-right corner. Product-detail page videos have separate rules: 16:9 or 9:16, 1–12 minutes, MOV or MP4, up to 1080p and 5 GB. AIVideosUGC makes 6, 10 or 15-second clips, which fit the Sponsored Brands duration but are shorter than the product-detail minimum. See Amazon Ads' Sponsored Brands video specs and Seller Central's product video guidance.

Amazon's main-image rules include a pure-white background and a product that fills at least 85% of the image. Check Seller Central's current main-image requirements, including pixel and zoom guidance.

faq.q: How should I order the images in an Amazon gallery?
faq.a: Start with the plain white-background main image, then add lifestyle, detail, scale or in-use views that answer the shopper's next question.

faq.q: Can the main Amazon image contain props or badges?
faq.a: Keep the main slot plain when the current category rules require it; put callouts, props and extra context on the secondary gallery images after checking Seller Central.

overview.h2: Treat the main image as a proof of the item
overview.d: A listing gallery works best when its square images answer different questions about this item. Lead with a clean white-background main image, then show a lifestyle view and a useful detail or size cue.

overview.h2: Use the gallery to answer the next questions
overview.d: Secondary images can show a close-up, a scale comparison, the parts in the box, and the product in a room. Sponsored Brands video specs call for 16:9 and 6–45 seconds. Product-detail videos are a separate placement and support 16:9 or 9:16, 1–12 minutes, and up to 1080p. AIVideosUGC's own clip options are 6, 10, or 15 seconds in five shapes. Check Amazon Ads' Sponsored Brands video specs and Seller Central's product-detail video guidance before uploading.

overview.h2: Give every gallery image a job
overview.d: A useful Amazon gallery moves from identification to proof. Use the white-background main image to show the complete item, a lifestyle view to show scale or setting, and detail or bundle views to answer a specific shopper question. Photograph or generate the same item from the same source reference so its proportions, color, and parts stay recognizable from slide to slide.

overview.h2: Separate Sponsored Brands from product-detail video
overview.d: Sponsored Brands video is an ad placement with its own 16:9 and duration rules. Product-detail video is uploaded to a product page and follows different duration, file, and resolution guidance. Choose the destination first, then make a file that fits that placement. A six, ten, or fifteen-second AIVideosUGC clip may fit an ad duration but does not satisfy a product-detail minimum that requires a longer video.

Put props, comparison views, callouts, and badges in secondary gallery slots when current category rules require a plain main image. Review the complete silhouette at seller preview size, confirm the product fills the frame without clipping, and add exact dimensions or claims in seller listing fields or a design editor after download.

overview.h2: Finish the listing set with variants and contents
overview.d: Use the front-facing white main image first, then add a same-item color comparison or a packaging-contents flatlay as secondary images. Keep props and callouts out of the main slot when the category requires a clean background, and verify each piece against the physical listing before upload.

input_guide.h2: Prepare a source for a trustworthy listing

items.d: Keep every part that ships with the product inside the frame. Do not expect a hidden side, cable, or accessory to appear accurately later.
For the main-image starting point, face the product toward the camera and keep the lens level so its proportions are easier to compare.
Take additional photos of the sole, clasp, ports, texture, or inside compartment when a shopper needs that information.
A square product view on clean white, with no extra words, badges, or props.
A square scene that shows this product in a familiar setting.
A square close view that shows a useful feature or size reference for this product.

scene_recipes.h2: Gallery scenes that answer shopper questions

items.d: Place a cutting board beside a mixing bowl on a kitchen counter, with a familiar mug nearby for context and no invented measurements.
Show a backpack standing upright with its main compartment open and the zipper, lining, and pockets visible.
Lay a watch or bag on a plain surface with the clasp, buckle, or stitching close enough to inspect.
Put a bath mat in front of a real-looking tub or a lamp on a side table, keeping the product's edges clear.

after_download.h2: Review every file before Seller Central

items.d: Check shape, color, parts, finish, and label against the physical product before you upload the asset.
Verify the pure-white background, product coverage, and pixel dimensions against Amazon's current category guidance.
Type dimensions, material names, prices, and feature labels yourself on secondary images, where the wording can be checked.
Remove props, added text, badges, and watermarks from the main image when the current rules require a clean product view.

fit.h2: Useful for an Amazon image set
good: Physical products with a clear, complete source photo
Listings that need a white main image plus detail and lifestyle frames
Sellers willing to verify the current category rules before upload
Products whose dimensions and claims can be added accurately after download
not_ideal: Items whose critical features are absent from every source photo
Claims that depend on an AI-generated label or measurement being exact
